summary: Lorenzo il Magnifico is a dense worker-placement game where dice-value workers claim action spaces to gather resources, buy cards, and race through developments across a shared board, with the twist that better dice values often mean worse placement order. Every turn is a tight optimization puzzle balancing short-term resource needs against long-term excommunication penalties and card-engine building, and this Big Box bundles the base game with several expansions adding new leaders, characters, and Pazzi Conspiracy cards for extra variability.
praised: Deep, satisfying worker-placement puzzle with meaningful dice-as-workers mechanic
Strong sense of engine-building and multiple viable strategies
High replayability from variable setup and modular expansion content
Excellent production values and thematic Renaissance art
criticised: Heavy rulebook and many symbols/exceptions make onboarding slow
Can suffer from analysis paralysis, especially at higher player counts
Excommunication tiles can feel punishing if a player falls behind
Some expansion content seen as adding complexity without proportional depth

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial via worker placement

scoring.why: Points come from military/territory/building/character cards, excommunication penalties, and end-game bonuses, so the winner is usually whoever built the most efficient multi-track engine.

similar: Marco Polo II: In the Service of the Khan
